body:
- [CALC] Recovery math: a −50% fall needs +100% to break even, −75% needs +300%, −90% needs +900%, and −94% (Amazon) needs about +1,567%. Leverage turns any of these drawdowns into permanent ruin. This is the link to Archegos and LTCM.
- Survivorship applies to temperament too. "Hold through a −90% drawdown" is good advice only for the Amazons. For the median dot-com IPO, it meant riding the stock to −85% and staying there. Holding needs conviction grounded in knowledge of the business, the Bezos "stock is not the company" view. Without that, holding is just stubbornness. The deciding variable is domain expertise, not a rule.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| DMart's permanent 70-300x P/E (`case_study:false-alarm-dmart-permanent-high-pe`) | high P/E; low FCF | owned-store real estate capex, EDLP model, negative-ish working capital, founder cost culture | ~11.7x from IPO Rs 299; ~5.4x from listing close | benign 2017-21; real at P/E >200 (2021) |
| Trent at 150-230x P/E with 'debt' jumping 10x (`case_study:false-alarm-trent-150x-pe-and-lease-debt`) | P/E 155+; debt 10x; loss year; ROCE 1% | COVID-depressed EPS; Ind AS 116 lease liabilities; visible store economics | ~19x (2020-24) | false alarm; exit signal was LFL, not P/E |
| Titan fails the CFO/PAT test and 'borrows' Rs 30,000 cr (`case_study:false-alarm-titan-negative-cfo-gold-loans`) | CFO/PAT 0.62 over 12 yrs; borrowings 300x | gold inventory + gold metal loans (natural hedge); low debtor days | ~12x (2015-26) | false alarm |
| Bajaj Finance's negative CFO every year and four QIPs (`case_study:false-alarm-bajaj-finance-negative-cfo-qips`) | negative CFO 12/12 yrs; 4 QIPs | lender accounting; growth equity at high P/B; promoter participation; ROE ~20% | ~32x (2015-26) | false alarm |
| Asian Paints, Pidilite, Page at 40-60x for 15+ years (`case_study:false-alarm-consumer-franchises-long-high-pe`) | P/E 40-60x for 15+ years | ROCE 25-60%, low debt, distribution moat, long runway | Asian Paints ~90x to 2022; Pidilite ~148x; Page ~197x | false alarm below ~1.5x own median; real above ~2x |
| Info Edge's reported losses and 3% ROCE (`case_study:false-alarm-info-edge-losses-low-roce`) | reported losses 4 years; ROCE 2-4% | high-margin core + venture portfolio accounting | ~40x (2006-26) | false alarm |
| Eternal (Zomato) losses, dilution and a 700x P/E (`case_study:false-alarm-eternal-zomato-losses-dilution`) | years of losses; dilution; 2-3% OPM; P/E ~712 | positive unit economics; growth QIP at high price; 1P revenue gross-up | ~4.8x from IPO; ~7.8x from 2022 low | false alarm at 2022 low; valuation risk now |
| Reliance's Jio-era debt doubling and ~10% ROCE (`case_study:false-alarm-reliance-jio-debt`) | debt doubled; ROCE 8-12% | capex ahead of near-certain demand, cash-generative core, stake sales, rights issue | ~5.9x (2016-26) | debt: false alarm; ROCE: partly real |
| Bharti Airtel's AGR losses, Rs 2 lakh cr debt and three equity raises (`case_study:false-alarm-bharti-airtel-losses-debt`) | losses FY20-21; debt 2.7x; ROCE 3%; rights+QIP | one-time AGR provision; CFO strong; spectrum dues; industry consolidation; promoter subscribed | ~7.4x (2019-26) | false alarm |
| APL Apollo's 5-8% operating margin (`case_study:false-alarm-apl-apollo-low-margins`) | OPM 5-8% | fast asset turns, ~0 WC days, ROCE 20-32%, share gains | ~670x (2009-26) | false alarm |
| HDFC Bank at 25-35x earnings and ~4x book (`case_study:false-alarm-hdfc-bank-expensive-bank`) | P/E 25-35; P/B several x | sustained ROE 16-20%, low NPA, CASA, long runway | ~35x (2005-26 peak) | false alarm 2005-2020; premium compressed after 2023 merger |
| Apollo Hospitals' 76% promoter pledge (`case_study:false-alarm-apollo-hospitals-promoter-pledge`) | promoter pledge ~68-78% of holding (2019) | family-level, disclosed purpose, falling via real stake sales, unlevered company, clean group | ~7x (2019-26) | false alarm, partly luck |
| HAL's 227 receivable days, negative CFO and salary borrowings (`case_study:false-alarm-hal-receivable-days`) | debtor days 227; CFO -Rs 7,700 cr; borrowings for salaries | sovereign counterparty, budget-timing delay, monopoly, order book | ~19x (2020-26) | false alarm |
| Amazon's missing profits and heavy capex (`case_study:false-alarm-amazon-no-profits-capex`) | no profits; high capex; meaningless P/E | negative WC, FCF/share focus, reinvestment, hidden AWS segment | ~2,500x (1997-2021) | business flag false; price flag true in 1999 |
| Netflix's -$3.3 bn free cash flow (`case_study:false-alarm-netflix-negative-fcf`) | FCF -$3.0bn (2018), -$3.27bn (2019); debt-funded | content library as capex; scale economics; pricing power; retention |  | false alarm |
| Tesla's losses and $12 bn of share sales (`case_study:false-alarm-tesla-losses-dilution`) | losses to 2020; $12bn equity in 2020; P/E >100 | survival risk resolved; raises at peak valuation ~1% each; funded capex | ~35x (2019-21) | survival flag false; valuation flag real |
| Costco's ~3% margin at 50-60x earnings (`case_study:false-alarm-costco-thin-margins-high-pe`) | ~3% net margin; P/E 48-60 | membership-fee profit model, negative WC, high ROIC, renewal ~90% | ~29x (2009-26) | margin flag false; valuation flag partly real |

*Method calibration, not stock picking. Research, not SEBI-registered advice.*
Started 2026-11-22. **Stage 3 (signals)** of `memory/roadmap.md`. It checks our one proven signal, the Indian PEAD
avoid leg (lessons L17, L19; `india_pead.md`, `india_pead_v2.md`). Both earlier tests drew their universe from
**today's** NSE equity list, so firms that died, were delisted or merged before Nov-2026 were absent (v1 §4: 16.8% of
Q3 FY19 filers are no longer listed). Lessons L27/L28: screener.in still serves dead Indian firms' weekly prices, and
survivors-only samples have already flipped one of our conclusions.
**Unlocks:** if the avoid leg holds with the dead firms back in, the stage-2/3 "avoid/exit after a big earnings miss"
rule keeps its proven status, and the live tracker's secondary test (`india_pead_live/`) is the right benchmark. If
it does not, the rule is downgraded before the live test starts in Jan-2027.
